svg.text: Power distribution network — 1.0 V FPGA core rail
The open risk flagged in the PCB floorplan, closed. The thermal land takes the area decoupling normally uses, so the decoupling ring sits 1.2 mm out. This is what that costs.
Lumped model to the package balls only. On-die capacitance takes over above roughly 200 MHz and is not modelled — which is why the analysis stops there.
ring at 1.2 mm — as floorplanned, ESL 0.50 nH
inside the ball shadow — ESL 0.30 nH, what the thermal land costs
no 0201 bank at all — what the ring is actually buying
individual banks: VRM, 22 µF, 4.7 µF, 0.1 µF, plane
Z = V × allowed ripple / transient step
The core rail is the binding one, so it is the one modelled.
2.8 V sensor analogue is not an impedance problem — it is a noise
problem, specified as < 1 mV RMS, 10 Hz – 10 MHz, at the array.
The ring placement passes, with margin.
36 mΩ at 200 MHz against a 100 mΩ target. Moving the
0201s inside the ball shadow would buy 11 mΩ. The
thermal land is worth more than 11 mΩ.
Deleting the ring does not pass.
121 mΩ at 200 MHz. The mid-frequency bank and the plane
pair between them do not cover the decade above 20 MHz —
The plane pair is nearly useless here.
70 pF is 11 Ω at 200 MHz. It contributes almost nothing
and is in the model only so nobody claims otherwise in
A real IBIS-AMI or on-die capacitance figure, and a
measured rather than assumed transient step. Both raise
the model above hand calculation — which is where it
